ov: A type of small horse, with a thicker coat, mane and tail, shorter legs, heavier bones and a wider body than larger horses. In most competitions a pony is any horse up to 14.2 hands (147 cm) at the withers when fully grown.
ht: Up to 14.2 hands (147 cm) at the withers
rg: Kept worldwide; ponies first developed as hardy landraces in harsh climates, typical of Northern Europe.
df: Hay and grass; ponies need about half the hay of a horse for their weight.

cf.tip: A pony is a small horse, not a young one: for competitions it measures 14.2 hands (147 cm) or less.

fx: Pound for pound, ponies can pull and carry more weight than a horse.
The word pony comes from the old French poulenet, a little foal.
notes: The animals.js fact is confirmed (a pony is fully grown and stays under 14.2 hands).
